notes:
Summary: StratusHealth is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for inference serving of clinical summarization and live triage assistant. Must meet strict residency and logging for PHI. Main negotiation focus is guaranteed throughput and burst handling rather than model selection.

Key technical asks (from infra & ML ops):
- Minimum sustained throughput guarantee requested: 120k tokens/sec aggregate for production cluster (covering 50% of weekday peak).
- Per-customer concurrency cap proposal: enforceable soft limit 400 concurrent chat sessions, hard cap 600; want automatic throttling behavior described.
- Burst policy: need documented burst credit pool for 2x sustained for up to 5 minutes per hour during clinic surges; must not exhaust KV cache priming budget.
- Reserved GPU planning: request mapping of reserved vGPU count -> expected tokens/sec (p95) across typical seq lengths (avg 256 tokens, max 2k). Want fallback model at 0.6x quality when capacity constrained.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile < 220ms for short-turn chat (<=128 tokens), 95th < 500ms for streaming long responses.

Sales / commercial notes:
- Procurement wants a capacity addendum to the MSA with specific minimum tokens/sec, concurrency caps, and weekday burst guarantees; also requests service credits for >1hr sustained breach.
- Pricing sensitivity: cost-per-1M tokens target around $12-$16 (post-quantization) for steady state; willing to pay 25% premium for hard 99.9% uptime SLA.

Recent touchpoints and shorthand:
- 2024-10-15: Intro call (Maya + Daniel) — high level requirements, asked for sizing spreadsheet.
- 2024-10-21: Technical deep dive (Daniel, Stratus infra team) — discussed KV cache, batching, and quantization. Fireflies id ff_012f9c_convo_20241021.
- 2024-11-05: Legal redlines received — heavy SLA/credits edits + data residency clause.
- 2024-11-12: Onsite demo of Dedicated runtime; ran synthetic load, saw 110k tokens/sec sustained at p95 with current config.
- 2024-11-18: Follow-up call to align burst semantics (Maya + Daniel + Stratus infra lead).

Customer quotes / color: "We need predictable throughput during clinic hours — a black box that spikes us into degraded UX is not acceptable."

Open technical action items:
- Provide mapping doc: reserved GPU counts -> expected tokens/sec by model variant and token length (target delivery 2024-11-27).
- Draft formal burst policy language: define credit accrual, max burst multiplier, behavior on exhaustion (queue vs reject).
- Provide sample SLA clause for procurement to review (include exact credit calculation).

POC metrics observed:
- Synthetic short-chat load (128 tokens avg): sustained 110k tokens/sec, p95 latency 210ms.
- Long-form streaming test (1k avg tokens): throughput drops to 40k tokens/sec, p95 latency 420ms.

Next steps (explicit):
- Maya to circulate Redwood draft capacity addendum to Stratus legal by 2024-11-22.
- SE to validate GPU sizing mapping and deliver by 2024-11-27.
- Commercial to prepare pricing tier with burst add-on and hard SLA option.
